newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada banks soar along with Canada dollar rally.
newsitem.headline: Canada banks soar along with Canada dollar rally.

text.p: Shares in Canadian banks jumped on Thursday as foreign investors stampeded into the Canadian market lured by a strong currency.
The six major banks moved closer to their all-time highs in heavy trading on the Toronto Stock Exchange as the Canadian dollar extended its recent rally on Thursday.
"They are pushing up to their old highs again. Technically, they look fantastic," said Dunnery Best, director of private client investing for Midland Walwyn Inc.
Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce led the charge, climbing 1.05 to 59 in turnover of 572,000 shares.
CIBC, Canada's second largest bank, is holding its annual general meeting in Vancouver today.
Among the other banks, Royal Bank of Canada gained 0.65 to 50.05 on 658,000 shares. Bank of Montreal improved 0.80 to 44.60 on 1.08 million shares.
Bank of Nova Scotia was the group's volume leader, adding 0.60 to 46.15 on 1.09 million shares.
Toronto-Dominion Bank rose 0.55 to 36.40 on 911,000 shares, while National Bank of Canada edged up 0.25 to 13.75 on 194,000 shares.

"If you have any confidence in the Canadian dollar, the best way for a foreigner to bet on it is to buy a Canadian bank. You've got dollar momentum and basically the same yield as a one year bond. It's a fantastic hedge on the currency," Best said in a telephone interview.
Soaring bank shares helped the TSE's key 300 Index break through the 6,100-point level earlier today. The 300 Index posted a record close on Wednesday helped by a bullish Canadian dollar.
The currency has strengthened more than two U.S. cents this year with analysts expecting further gains this week.
Stock analysts said Canadian bank shares are also getting a lift from strong U.S. bank earnings this week.
Several U.S. bank holding companies have posted fourth quarter earnings 10 percent or higher than year-earlier results.
